name: juise
why: A scripting environment for Juniper JUNOS that opens an unusual door into router config automation, though barely used.

brief.what_it_is: JUISE (JUNOS User Interface Scripting Environment) is a set of tools for writing, testing and debugging SLAX scripts that run on Juniper's JUNOS software, using a desktop machine instead of the router. Its README says it lets scripts be developed and run outside the normal JUNOS environment, with a debugger, profiler, call-flow tracing and trace files. Scripts can call JUNOS XML data through the jcs:invoke and jcs:execute functions, and commit scripts can be tested against a device's configuration. The fetched pages do not name the executables' inputs or outputs in detail; the brew metadata lists the binaries juise and juise-config.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the goal is to let users develop scripts in their desktop environment and run the code/test/debug cycle in a more natural way than on the device itself.
brief.how_it_works: The README describes JUNOS-specific extension functions that give scripts access to JUNOS XML data through jcs:invoke and jcs:execute, and says commit scripts can be run against a device's configuration to check their results on that device. Release notes for 0.6.0 say jcs:execute and related calls use a 'mixer' process as the connection manager to the device. The README does not explain the mechanism in detail.
brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, the release notes show a source build with autotools (configure, Makefile.am, autoreconf) and a dependency on libslax; a 0.6.0 note says it required libslax-0.18.0 and a 3.0.0 note mentions moving to libslax-0.22.0. The optional mixer component needs libssh2 and libsqlite3 when built with --enable-mixer. The wiki's 'Building juise' page is linked but was not fetched, so I did not read the build steps.
brief.standout: It is an offline SLAX test harness for JUNOS commit scripts, so script logic can be debugged on a laptop before it touches a router. Release 0.9.0 added the ability to run sh, perl and python scripts, not only SLAX.
brief.status: Quiet. The wiki's most recent news item is dated 2013-08-20 and the homepage shows nothing newer. The latest GitHub release is juise-3.0.0, dated only as '01 Apr' with no year visible in the fetched text. The earlier releases are dated 2013 and before. I could not confirm a recent commit date.
brief.caveats: The README is thin and mostly points to the wiki. Most wiki links (manual, introduction, building) had no URLs in the fetched text, so I did not read them. The project is tied to SLAX and libslax, and the older Clira web front end was built on PHP-free Ember.js code that is dated to about 2013-2014. The license is a Juniper-held LICENSE file referenced in the Copyright file, and I did not see a named open-source license. The release notes mention Mac, Cygwin, Debian and RPM packaging, but nothing on current platform support. The brew description says the project is barely used.

allows scripts to be written, debugged, and executed outside the normal JUNOS environment.
Commit scripts can be tested against a JUNOS device's configuration and the results of those script tested on that device.
